# screen recording and resubmission protocol — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for screen recording and resubmission protocol. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-02 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] Resubmitting closes the Resolution Center line of communication, so the safe order is: reply with evidence (e.g. screen recording), wait for the reviewer to confirm or answer, then resubmit only if a code or metadata change is needed. Replies without resubmitting do get answers in practice, but replying alone does not necessarily trigger a fresh review cycle. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/743567 · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/app-store-metadata-rejected

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Apple's help text does not document file-size limits, accepted video formats, or whether a link versus an uploaded file is preferred for screen recordings; the pages checked state only that other file types are allowed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-submissions-to-app-review/reply-to-app-review-messages/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Apple's Resolution Center reply lets Account Holder, Admin, or App Manager roles send up to 4,000 characters and attach files (screenshots, supporting documents) to a rejection reply; the thread stays open only until the developer resubmits to App Review. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-submissions-to-app-review/reply-to-app-review-messages/ · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256
- [statement] A metadata-rejected submission can be fixed by editing the cited metadata and resubmitting the same build; a binary rejection requires uploading and selecting a new build. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-submissions-to-app-review/reply-to-app-review-messages/ · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/app-store-metadata-rejected
- [statement] For features hard to reproduce in review (hardware, special environments, unusual behaviour), Apple expects a demo video or the hardware; a video can be attached via the Attachment field in App Review Information, with explanations or links in Review Notes. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/ · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/the-ultimate-guide-to-app-store-rejections
- [statement] Apple's FAQ says screenshots may be attached to the Resolution Center reply to show how the app addresses the rejection, and that the Notes/attachments in App Review Information can explain where reviewers find specific features; this applies to a menu-bar app with no main window. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256 · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/the-ultimate-guide-to-app-store-rejections
- [statement] Appeals go to the App Review Board through App Store Connect: give specific reasons the app complies, submit one appeal per rejected submission, and answer any pending information request before appealing. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review/ · keywords: screen recording and resubmission protocol · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256
- [statement] Apple generally responds to Resolution Center messages within about 24 hours, but forum reports describe repetitive copy-paste replies that ignore the developer's specific question. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/743567
